discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental realization of topological insulators, including the quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects

nominees.name: Qikun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) and Tsinghua University, China

motivation: Topological insulators revealed that band topology, not only symmetry breaking, defines new phases of matter with protected, dissipationless edge and surface states. Charles Kane formulated the Z2 topological invariant that defines the quantum spin Hall insulator and its three-dimensional generalization. Laurens Molenkamp, through exquisite molecular-beam epitaxy of HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, gave the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect in 2007. Qikun Xue, again through atomically controlled MBE growth of magnetically doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 thin films, achieved in 2013 the long-sought quantum anomalous Hall effect: quantized Hall conductance without any external magnetic field. Together these works show how theoretical insight and mastery of crystal growth create entirely new quantum states, now underpinning research on low-dissipation electronics, metrology and topological quantum computation.
